result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give all ten events a treatment and keep push for the cancellation, the card problem and urgent delay or gate changes. B is better on the automatic rebooking: its sample message says what changed and offers a different flight. A only promises the new itinerary and gives no way to review or change it. Both drop the 'found none' message and demote promotions, and both offer category-level controls instead of ten toggles. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give all ten events a treatment and keep push for cancellations, the card problem, and delays or gate changes that matter. A wins on the rebooking message: its example says what changed and invites the traveler to pick a different flight. B only says to send the new itinerary. B explains each choice more fully and adds useful ideas like collapsing repeated updates and quiet hours, but it doesn't close the review-and-change gap.
